answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to lock a small, refundable copper-weighted stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed if peers later prove fraud. New identities start with no reputation, like a bare reef that must slowly grow coral: they can only handle tiny tasks until honest completions accumulate. A single sonnet of self-praise earns nothing; only verifiable work history unlocks larger deals, so creating thousands of fake agents costs more in locked capital and time than any attack could recover.
